text:
sam: quick PSA - examples/quickstart/README.md still shows `REDWOOD_API_KEY` and the old JS `client.generate()` call. copy/paste hazard for new users.

sam: current snippet:

```
# bad
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-XXXX
node -e "const { Redwood } = require('redwood'); const c = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); c.generate('hello').then(r => console.log(r.text))"
```

lee: thanks. which SDK version does this target?

sam: looks like an older example. our guidance is `REDWOOD_KEY`, constructor takes no `apiKey` arg, and method is `create_completion` in modern samples.

andra: can you open a tiny PR to replace with `.env.example` usage, change to `REDWOOD_KEY`, and swap method names? also replace `sk-XXXX` with `REDACT_ME` placeholder.

sam: opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/pull/450 - changes README, adds `.env.example`, and updates wording about not including secrets.

ci-bot: [CI] examples-lint failed on commit b1c2d3: forbidden token `REDWOOD_API_KEY` found in examples/quickstart/README.md - see CI log

lee: nice - add a grep-based CI check so future regressions fail fast.

andra: we should also discuss a lightweight snippet smoke test that runs each snippet with fake creds to ensure function names/imports don't drift. filing issue after merge.

sam: updated PR per feedback; CI green. merging now.

docs-bot: docs-pr-reviewer assigned andra to PR 450

andra: merged. follow-up issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/issues/219 - "snippet smoke tests + forbidden-token lint"

sam: thanks all. small fix, big impact.
